# Claru (claru.ai)

Fetched: 2026-07-16
URL: https://claru.ai

## Page inventory

1. **Homepage** (/) — Tagline, value props, CTAs. ~2-3 min
2. **/about** — Mission, problem statement, capabilities, organizational structure, investor backing. ~2 min
3. **/compare** — Positioning vs 70+ competitors across categories. Comparison table/grid visible. ~4 min
4. **/datasets** — Directory landing with searchable open-source dataset index (1000+ datasets claimed), plus Claru proprietary collections. Filter by modality, robot platform, environment, task. ~3 min
5. **/datasets/{name}** — Individual dataset pages (example: thermal-industrial). Card format with specs, metrics, modalities, use cases. ~2 min each
6. **/training-data/{name}** — Training data offering pages (example: packing). Problem statement, solution specs, metrics, compatible models, CTAs. ~2 min each
7. **/solutions/{name}** — Solution pages (example: teleoperation-data). Problem/solution narrative with scale metrics. ~3 min
8. **/glossary** — 56 terms organized in 7 categories. Definitions with technical depth. ~3 min
9. **/blog** — 15 posts, recent from Apr-May 2026. Categories: physical AI, VLA, diffusion policy, sim-to-real, egocentric video, data enrichment, humanoid robots. ~1 min to scan
10. **/jobs** — Job listing directory (game-testing-annotator, game-data-collector visible). Individual job pages with specs, rate, location. ~1 min
11. **/app/signup** — Signup flow (not fetched in detail)
12. **/pricing** — Returns 404; no public pricing page exists

## Homepage section order

1. Hero/Tagline: "Training Data for Physical AI"
2. Scale & Breadth: "Millions of clips. Every environment." + description of data types (egocentric, game, driving, manufacturing)
3. Data Enrichment: "More than video. Captured, enriched, annotated, and delivered to your pipeline." + technical layers (depth, pose, segmentation)
4. Global Collection Network: "10,000+ collectors. 100+ cities. Every environment your model needs." + six continents claim
5. Proven Track Record: "Built for frontier labs. Proven at scale." + three metric claims (500K+ egocentric videos, 2M+ annotations, 100+ active datasets)
6. Service Offering: "Tell us what you are training." + "From brief to first delivery in days, not months."
7. CTAs: "Book a Call" button + email ([email protected])

## Proof placement

Scale metrics (500K+ videos, 2M+ annotations, 100+ datasets):
- Listed on homepage "Proven Track Record" section, same page as claims
- Repeated on /about page with same numbers
- No external citations, no links to evidence

Collector/city claims (10,000+, 100+):
- Listed on homepage section 4
- Repeated on /about page in "Global Collection Network" description
- No sourcing provided

"1000 open-source datasets":
- Listed on /datasets page hero section
- Claim appears unverified; no enumeration visible in search results

Individual dataset metrics (25K+ clips, 180+ hours for thermal-industrial):
- Specified on individual dataset page (/datasets/thermal-industrial)
- Accompanied by facility types, equipment categories, annotation layers
- Specific quality targets cited (95%+ equipment ID, 92%+ anomaly classification)

Comparison claims vs competitors:
- /compare page states Claru is "only company 100% focused on physical AI"
- Positioned against Scale AI, Appen, Labelbox, Luel, Surge AI with differentiation language
- No comparative metrics provided; only architectural/functional differences cited

## Claim qualification

"100% focused on physical AI" — Unqualified positioning claim without scope delimiter (vertical focus, not market share)

"only company" — Strong absolute; structure is hedged slightly with domain qualifier but remains categorical

"Proven at scale" — Qualified by three metrics, but metrics lack external validation or timestamping

"more than labels" vs Scale AI — Functional differentiation without performance comparison

"from brief to first delivery in days, not months" — Service speed claim without baseline or reference project scope

"gold standard for robot demonstration data" — Applied to teleoperation on /solutions/teleoperation-data; attributed to method, not to Claru specifically

"5-10x fewer robot demonstrations when pre-training on diverse human video data" — Specific ratio claim on teleoperation page without citation or methodology reference

Individual dataset quality targets (95%+, 92%+) — Precise thresholds without external auditing reference

## Type and color

Design system details not accessible via text extraction from WebFetch. Color values (hex/RGB) not visible in available content. Font family names not specified in retrieved markup. Button styling visible as text labels only ("Book a Call", "Request a Sample Pack", email links). Page uses hierarchical heading structure with emphasis blocks for key metrics.

## Conversion path

**Homepage:** CTAs are "Book a Call" button + email contact
**Datasets page:** "Request a Sample Pack" or "Browse the Data Catalog"
**Training-data pages:** "Get in Touch" or "Browse the Data Catalog"
**Solutions pages:** Email contact form (name, email, company, use case, referral)
**Jobs pages:** "Apply in minutes" via profile creation

First touchpoint is always descriptive (use case, benefits, metrics) before CTA. No email capture gate at entry; CTAs are explicit conversion requests (call, sample request, application).

## Distinctive

Two page farms stand out:
1. **/datasets** directory with individual dataset cards (thermal-industrial, etc.) combining index architecture with detailed spec pages. Each card shows clip count, facility types, annotation layers, quality metrics (95%+ agreement targets), and use cases. Search/filter by modality, robot platform, environment, task.
2. **/training-data** pages (packing, etc.) structured as problem-solution narratives with specific metrics (72.1% volume utilization, 5B+ annual packages), compatible ML models listed by name (Diffusion Policy, SpatialVLM, PackIt), and environment types enumerated.

Both page farms demonstrate confidence in specificity: they cite equipment categories (50+), anomaly types (12), facility types (10+), modalities (thermal, RGB-D, LiDAR, IMU, force-torque, event-camera, point-cloud), and annotation quality targets with numeric precision.

## Noise

Heavy reliance on category terminology without differentiation:
- "frontier labs", "physical AI", "embodied AI", "VLA models", "world models" appear repeatedly across pages
- These terms are category language; competitors likely use identical terminology
- /glossary dedicates an entire resource to defining these terms, which may signal market education need or territory claim, but the definitions themselves are standard (VLA as "neural network that takes visual observations and language instructions as input")
- /blog post titles lean heavily on buzzwords (e.g., "π₀.₇ Foundation Model: Steerable Emergent Robot Capabilities 2026")
